props.title: Fantasia

sections.content: **Fantasia** (1940) revolutionized the marriage of classical music and animation, creating a landmark experimental film that Disney would never quite match again. Walt Disney's ambitious vision paired Leopold Stokowski conducting the Philadelphia Orchestra with abstract animation, nature scenes, and mythological sequences. The film's centerpiece, **The Sorcerer's Apprentice** segment with Mickey Mouse, remains one of Disney's most iconic sequences, but it's the daring "Rite of Spring" sequence depicting evolution and dinosaurs that showcases the studio's willingness to tackle complex themes through animation.

sections.content: The technical innovations of Fantasia pushed animation boundaries, introducing the "Fantasound" system - an early form of surround sound. The film's influence extends to experimental works like **Pink Floyd - The Wall** (1982) and modern music-driven animations like **Interstella 5555** (2003). The "Night on Bald Mountain" sequence particularly influenced dark fantasy animation, echoing in films like **The Black Cauldron** (1985) and **Princess Mononoke** (1997).

While commercially unsuccessful in its initial release, Fantasia's artistic ambition paved the way for mature animation targeting adult audiences. The abstract "Toccata and Fugue" sequence influenced experimental animators like Oskar Fischinger and Norman McLaren, while the pastoral "Pastoral Symphony" sequence's mythological elements resonated through Disney's later works like **Hercules** (1997). sections.content: Fantasia's DNA can be found in countless music-driven animated features, from **Dumbo** (1941) to modern works like **Coco** (2017). The film's "Dance of the Hours" sequence, featuring ballet-dancing hippos and alligators, established Disney's tradition of anthropomorphized animals performing classical music, influencing sequences in **Beauty and the Beast** (1991) and **The Princess and the Frog** (2009).
